pageCache.pageTitle: Stanton Harcourt Primary School – Living, Learning and Growing Together.
pageCache.text:
Stanton Harcourt CE Primary School
Headteacher’s Welcome
A very warm welcome to Stanton Harcourt CE Primary School. As a small school we get to know our children and families very well and our pastoral systems promote the development of excellent relationships between pupils and the whole staff team. The children have a strong sense of belonging to a school family and by the time they leave us at the end of Year 6, they are responsible, independent young people, and we are very proud of them.
As a Church of England primary school, our vision is rooted in the Bible verse in Romans 12:4, “Each one of us has a body, and that body has many parts… In Christ we are all one body and we are all a part of it. Each part belongs to all the other parts. We all have different gifts.” We embrace the diversity of gifts, skills, and qualities within our school community. Together, we live, learn, and grow in a nurturing environment that cherishes each individual, enabling the whole body to flourish.
Through our curriculum, we aim high for all, offering both challenge and support so that every child can grow in confidence, character and capability. We believe that by recognising and nurturing each child’s individual strengths, they can achieve their full potential – academically, socially and spiritually.
We enable children to understand their place in the world, who they are and how they can serve others. We actively create opportunities for service to others, helping children understand the values of compassion, kindness, support and friendship.
Our wider curriculum is designed to develop responsible and inclusive global citizens. We help children understand the wider world and their place in it, encouraging them to embrace difference, celebrate diversity, and act justly and wisely.
Our school is very much part of our local community, and we welcome the community into school in roles such as reading volunteers.
We endeavour to work in partnership with parents, as we know this allows children to flourish. We have many events throughout the year to support parents and work with them to allow all of our children to reach their full potential.
Our curriculum aims to give our children rich learning opportunities and valuable experiences, to encourage them to be life long, inquisitive learners. We believe it is integral to children’s development to understand their place within the school community and relate this to a much wider global community, thus providing the children with experiences and knowledge of different world religions and faiths so that they can become tolerant, compassionate citizens. We aspire for our children to leave their primary education having the integrity, values and inspiration to enter the next step of their journey with confidence and embrace and influence the world that they live in.
Stanton Harcourt CE Primary School is part of the EPA Trust, an academy made up of a large 11-19 outstanding secondary school, an all-through primary/secondary school, and ten primary schools which host five nurseries. The EPA family of schools is dedicated to high academic achievement and developing well-rounded children. Our schools enable children to become successful learners, confident individuals and responsible citizens.
If your child is due to start school in September 2027 please contact the office on 01865 881948 or office.3130@stantonharcourtschool.org.uk to book an appointment to look around. We have two tours for prospective reception/nursery parents on the following dates:
Tuesday 20th October 2026 at 10am
Tuesday 1st December at 10am
Please contact the school office if you would like to join one of these tours.
If you would like your child to join the school during the year in other year groups please get in touch. We will look forward to welcoming you to our school.
Testimonials
“Pupils thrive in this vibrant and respectful environment. Staff’s high expectations for behaviour create a calm and orderly atmosphere. Pupils not only get along well but also embrace learning with enthusiasm. Pupils’ positive attitudes stem from the school’s vision, ‘Living, Learning, and Growing Together’, which nurtures a strong sense of belonging.”
“The Christian values drive every aspect of the school’s work to ensure that every pupil achieves to the best of their ability in an extremely supportive and nurturing environment. Relationships between pupils and adults are strong so that pupils feel completely safe and cared for as individuals. “
“Relationships between staff and pupils are built on mutual respect and support. Pupils feel valued and know their voices are heard.”
“Teachers’ strong subject knowledge and clear presentation within lessons helps pupils to explain their ideas and remember what they learn. Support for pupils with SEND is a key part of the school’s approach, with needs identified quickly. Effective adjustments are made to ensure that they can learn alongside their peers.”

Governance
The Governors work closely with Mrs Tingley (Headteacher) and staff at Stanton Harcourt CE Primary School and form the Local Governing Board (LGB) for the school. Stanton Harcourt CE Primary School is part of the Eynsham Partnership Academy Trust and the EPA scheme of delegation https://www.epa-mat.org/schemes-of-delegation/ sets out the roles, structure and responsibilities of the LGB.
In conjunction with school leadership, the LGB are responsible for:-
Governors are assigned specific areas of responsibility within the school (please see schedule for details). Governors are also allocated curriculum areas, for which they liaise regularly with subject leads, visit to observe teaching and report back to the LGB.
Governors are appointed by the EPA for their skills and experience in education and leadership, as well as from parents/carers and staff.
LGB meetings are held termly (please see schedule for details of attendance).

We contract a company called Dolce to provide fresh, hot food for the children’s lunches.
Menus
Reload document | Open in new tab
Free School Meals
If you or your partner receives Income Support, ESA (IR), Income-based Jobseekers Allowance or Child Tax Credit (not Working Tax Credit) & have a family income below £16,190 you may be eligible for a FREE school meal.
If your child is eligible they will receive a tasty, nutritious school lunch free every day of the school year. Once registered, your school will also receive additional funding which will help your child. The provision of a free school lunch is discreet and anonymous in the dining room. If you think that you might be eligible please do come and see the school office as all we need is your name, date of birth and National Insurance Number and we can check whether you fit the criteria.
Universal Free School Meals
As from September 2014 all children in Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 are entitled to a free school meal every day.
Did you know that registering your child for Free School Meals, even if they would receive them anyway through the Universal Free School Meals Plan means that the school gets extra money from the Government. For every child registered the school gets £1,300 extra support. Please register so that our school doesn’t miss out on vital money to spend on your child’s education.
